Delay is condoned.
It appears that the present appellants nos.2 and 4 were minor at the time of filing of the claim application and during the pendency of the instant appeal they became major.
So, after attaining the age of majority, it is necessary to note in the Memo of the Appeal to consider them to be a major.
It further appears that the name of the appellant no.4 was erroneously mentioned as 'Anan Kahar' the correct name of the appellant no.4 should be recorded as 'Anal Kahar'.
The department is made out the above mentioned corrections in the cause title of the Memo of the appeal accordingly.

The instant appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated July 13, 2009 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Fast Track, 2 nd Court, Paschim Midnipur in M.A.C. Case No. 17 of 2007 under Section 166 of the M. V. Act.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The present appellants being the claimants preferred the application u/s 166 of the Act before the learned Tribunal for getting compensation on the ground that their predecessor was died in a road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
The Insurance Company contested the matter before the learned Tribunal.

The evidence were adduced, the documentary evidences were taken on record as separate exhibit numbers and after hearing the parties, the learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,40,000/- in favour of the claimants.

Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said award, the present claimants have preferred this Basanti Kahar & Ors vs Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Anr on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132300464/
1 appeal for enhancement of the claim amount.

entities.text: Basanti Kahar & Ors vs Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The sole point involved in this appeal is the monthly income of the deceased.

Learned advocate for the appellants submitted before this Court that the learned Tribunal without considering the materials on record and without considering the evidences have assessed the compensation amount considering the annual income of the deceased to be Rs.15,000/- notionally.

He further argued that the deceased used to earn Rs.4,000/- per month for selling cosmetic goods,
perfume from door to door at quarters of Airforce, Kalaikunda and also in other villages.
He also submitted that the evidences to that effect has already been adduced which was corroborated the pleadings of the claimant.
So, he prayed for necessary order, so that the compensation of this case may be assessed considering the income of the deceased Rs.4,000/- per month.
Learned advocate for the Insurance Company raised strong objection and submitted before this Court that there are no palpable error in the impugned award passed by the learned Tribunal.
No documentary evidences were adduced to justify the claim of the appellants.
He also submitted that the only claim before the learned Tribunal regarding the income of the deceased does not ipso facto proved to be the income of the deceased raised Rs.4,000/- per month.

So, he also pointed out that statutory reduction towards the personal expenses of the deceased was also not deducted and the miltiplier adopted by the learned Tribunal is erroneous considering the age of the deceased within the age group of 35 to 40.
Heard the learned advocates.
Perused the impugned judgment and also the paper book containing the evidences recorded by the learned Tribunal.
In considering the evidences on record, it is true that there are no documentary evidences regarding the income of the deceased.
Thus, the income of the deceased should be considered notionally.
It is the practice of the Court that the notional income of a deceased, who died in a road traffic accident up to year 2010 is considered, Rs.3,000/- per month.
So, in this case, I think it is necessary that the impugned award should be modified to that effect that the monthly income of the deceased should be Rs.3,000/- per month.

According to the direction of the Hon'ble Supreme Court passed in Pranay Shetty, the claimants are also entitled to get future prospects i.e. 40% of his established income and general damages Rs.30,000/-.
Considering the entire aspect, the award passed by the learned Tribunal is hereby modified.

Thus the award of compensation is as follows:
1. Monthly income be assessed as Rs.3000/-
2. Annual income be assessed as Rs.36000/-
3. Deduction 1/4th (-) Rs.9000/-

Balance Compensation Rs.3,57,000/-
The Insurance Company is directed to pay the balance compensation amounting to Rs.3,57,000/-to the claimants along with 6% interest per annum from the date of filing of the claim application i.e.
from January 9, 2007.

The insurance Company is further directed to deposit the amount with the office of the learned Tribunal within eight weeks from the date of passing of this order in the name of the appellant/claimants vide four equal account payee cheques subject to the ascertainment of payment of requisite Court fees.
On such deposit, the claimants are at liberty to withdraw the same according to the prevalent rules.
Accordingly, FMAT 385 of 2010 is disposed of.
All connected applications, if any, are also disposed of.
Return the LCR at once.
All parties shall act on the server copy of this order duly downloaded from the official website of this Court.
